A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 68-page versions of the same work, with matching sections and Appendices A–K. Text and visual comparisons support reliable assessment; all 58 appendix pages are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original travel-planning simulations measuring privacy leakage, security attack success, and utility in Tables 2–6, with qualitative results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original simulation results in Tables 2–6 and the qualitative examples in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix G retain the same construction of rules from prior simulations and the same input, data, and trajectory firewalls. The procedures, components, and implementation prompts are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic travel-planning environment, four personas, benign adaptation scenarios, privacy attacks, calendar-deletion attack, and upselling attack. The profiles and travel options in Appendices B and D are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 retain the Baseline, Task-confined, and Firewalled (D + T) comparisons. Table 6 retains the same task-confined and firewall configurations, including improved rules and the input firewall; no comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 retain the same LLM-as-a-Judge procedures, metrics, GPT-4o model version gpt-4o-2024-11-20, and top-p setting of 0.92. The one-persona versus all-persona rule-generation experiments and attack procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The firewall-component and rule-update comparisons are retained without modification. Section 6.5, Appendix A's attack examples, and Appendices J–K's benign conversation cases contain the same analyses and evidence.

E5.justification: Section 6.2 reports the same ten repetitions, 40 runs across personas per experiment, 1080 total runs, and averaging procedure. Neither version adds seed disclosure, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 and the appendix examples retain their results. For example, Table 3 reports medical-data leakage of 70%, 35%, and 0% for Baseline, Task-confined, and Firewalled (D + T) in both versions; Table 4 likewise retains calendar-deletion attack success rates of 45%, 22%, and 0%.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the conditional-subgoal notation, interaction assumptions, and threat-model definitions. No mathematical reasoning, formal result, or proof is introduced, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: defining requirements for adaptable agentic networks, constructing a travel-planning testbed, identifying privacy and security risks, and proposing layered firewalls. Their scope and effectiveness claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of firewall generalization and complementary protection remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning evaluation without ground truth, potentially vulnerable input sanitization, data abstraction restricting further reasoning, and incomplete protection against trajectory-dependent attacks.

D1.justification: v3 removes the first-page statement 'Code is going to be available soon' while retaining the same repository link. This removes code-availability information but does not establish that code was released. Experimental settings and the extensive appendix implementation documentation are unchanged.

R1.justification: The task-drift reference changes from 'Get my drift? catching llm task drift with activation deltas' (SaTML, 2025) to 'Are you still on track!? catching llm task drift with activations' (arXiv, 2024), with the same authors and contextual role. This is a title/publication-metadata update for the matched work; cited-work coverage and research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes Eugene Bagdasarian and the corresponding University of Massachusetts Amherst affiliation, adds Amr Gomaa's BMBF/FedWell funding acknowledgment, and updates bibliographic text and citation labels. These are limited edits; the scientific prose and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened front matter and added acknowledgment cause limited column and page reflow, including shifted reference entries. Figures 1–3 and the tables retain their designs and content, and the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the methods, results, scientific argument, limitations, and complete appendix documentation. The funding acknowledgment adds a small disclosure benefit, while the other edits concern attribution, bibliography, and layout. Removing the forthcoming-code note does not establish improved access or reproducibility, so the revision provides no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
